page.layout: One page of text: a block of italic Latin verse in the upper half, a signature "A. F." at the right below it, a printer's ornament in the middle of the lower page, and a gathering mark "B. ij." at the foot. No margin notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top right.

p.i: Angusto Isacidas ipfa Pharos finu Urgebat: spatiis omnibus imminens Hostilis facies te, Anglia, cinxerat.
At caeli facies, Anglia, te tegit, Cernit te placidis luminibus Deus, Cingit moenibus & te Deus igneis, Undis non aliter quàm bene cingeris.
Ast ut moenibus his cingeris, Anglia, Cingentem celebra continuo Deum, Capit vorticibus qui dare debitis Hispanas acies, & gregibus vagis Protei Cannibalos expofuit truces.
Sic, Regina, tuum condecoret caput: Sic firmet Solium: sic populum DEVS: Cui, Regina, tuum cum Solio caput Debes & populum: cunctaque cui refers.

page.notes: The printer's ornament in the lower middle of the page is a decorative fleuron, not text, and is not transcribed. "Angusto Isacidas ipfa Pharos finu" reads as printed; the first word may be "Angusto" or "Augusto" [?] but the print is clearly "Angusto". "DEVS" is set in small capitals within the verse. Show-through from the reverse is visible on the right and is omitted. The page number "21" at top right is partly worn; read as 21 with doubt.
